meta.title: Least-cost Network & Logistics Optimization | Sāra 0003 | TriSaar Consulting
meta.description: Sāra 0003 case study: a network optimization and Excel/VBA decision-support tool that calculates total delivered cost and ranks alternative plants for each city, product and channel.
meta.author: TriSaar Consulting

data.text: Turning freight, clinker, subsidy and variable-cost data into a ranked view of the lowest-cost plants for every market.

A network optimization tool that combines freight, clinker, subsidy, production and variable costs to calculate total delivered cost and surface the top plant alternatives for each city, product and channel.

data.title: One view of the lowest-cost plant for every market.
data.subtitle: A repeatable total delivered cost engine for evaluating plant-to-market allocation.

pillars.label: Challenge
pillars.title: The lowest-cost option was difficult to identify at network scale.
pillars.body: With dozens of plants, multiple products and hundreds of cities, identifying the best plant for a market often meant manually checking freight rates, existing plant-to-city assignments and inputs from different teams.

points.text: Multiple cost components across the network
Alternative-plant analysis depended on manual coordination

pillars.label: Solution
pillars.title: A total delivered cost engine for network-wide plant selection.
pillars.body: We built a decision-support tool that combines the relevant cost components and ranks the top 5 plant alternatives for a selected city, product and channel.

steps.text: Combines production, clinker, freight, subsidy & variable costs
Calculates total delivered cost across the network
Tests cost scenarios by toggling subsidy and variable-cost assumptions

pillars.label: Impact
pillars.title: From manual alternative-plant analysis to structured network decisions.
pillars.body: The team can now evaluate the lowest-cost plant and the next-best alternatives from a consistent cost view, helping them respond faster when a preferred plant is affected by logistics, manufacturing or natural-hazard disruptions.

parts.text: The client moved from ad-hoc, plant-by-plant comparisons to an
structured ranking of the lowest-cost and next-best plant options
for each city, product and channel.

data.title: Finding the next-best plant was a manual network exercise.
data.body: The production network spanned dozens of plants, products and hundreds of cities. When the preferred plant was not viable because of a logistics issue, manufacturing constraint or natural hazard, teams had to manually investigate alternative plants using freight rates, existing assignments and guidance from colleagues.

core.label: The Core Challenge
core.body: The data needed to evaluate plant economics existed, but there was no consistent network-wide decision view that quickly ranked the best alternatives for a market.

points.title: Complex network choices
points.body: Each decision could involve multiple plants, products, cities and channels, creating thousands of possible plant-to-market combinations.

points.title: Manual cost checking
points.body: Teams checked freight rates, existing plant-to-city assignments and other cost inputs across different sources before comparing alternatives.

points.title: Colleague-dependent analysis
points.body: Finding the right alternative often relied on guidance and knowledge from colleagues familiar with the network, rather than a common decision framework.

points.title: Limited alternative visibility
points.body: The lowest-cost option might be clear only after manual analysis, while the next-best alternatives were harder to assess quickly when circumstances changed.

impact.label: The Business Impact
impact.body: When a preferred plant became constrained or unavailable, the business could struggle to act quickly. Manual alternative analysis was time-consuming, plant allocation could remain suboptimal, and decisions could depend on individual knowledge and colleague guidance.

data.title: A network-wide engine for total delivered cost and plant ranking.
data.intro: We translated the client's network economics into a repeatable Excel/VBA decision-support tool. Users select a city, product and channel; the engine calculates total delivered cost across relevant plants and surfaces the top alternatives for comparison.

hub.label: Our Approach
hub.body: Convert fragmented cost & network into one consistent framework for evaluating plant-to-market economics.

steps.title: Bring the network economics together
steps.body: Consolidated the cost inputs required to evaluate each plant-to-market combination across production, clinker, freight, subsidy and variable cost.

steps.title: Calculate total delivered cost
steps.body: Built a consistent calculation for each plant, city, product and channel combination so alternatives could be compared on the same economic basis.

steps.title: Rank the network alternatives
steps.body: For a selected city, product and channel, the tool evaluates the network and ranks the top 5 plant options by total delivered cost.

steps.title: Support scenario-based decisions
steps.body: Users can test the effect of cost assumptions, including whether subsidy is considered and how variable cost from additional demand changes the ranking.

items.title: Network-wide visibility
items.body: The economics of plant alternatives can be assessed through one consistent view.

items.title: Alternatives surfaced
items.body: The next-best plants are visible alongside the lowest-cost option.

items.title: Faster response
items.body: Teams can evaluate alternatives without repeating a plant-by-plant manual analysis.

enablers.label: Key Enablers
enablers.intro: The tool combines network economics with lightweight Excel automation.

data.title: Faster alternative evaluation. Better-informed network decisions.
data.intro: The tool turned a fragmented, manually guided exercise into a structured decision-support process for evaluating plant-to-market alternatives.

bridge.quote: When the preferred plant changes, the next-best option should not require starting the analysis from scratch.
